content: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Mon, 09 Nov 2026 21:57:06 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.12 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/october-2026-unicorn-board-gains-34-tops-1900-ai-defense/ Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:00:34 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94362 A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The board also reached a new record of 1,900 private companies last month, including an all-time high of more than 1,000 such startups based in the U.S. Last month’s new unicorn cohort also highlighted how quickly this AI cycle is awarding some companies with billion-dollar-plus valuations: Half of October’s new unicorns are less than 4 years old, and nine companies that joined the board during the month did so via seed or Series A raises. Leading industries for unicorn formation last month were frontier labs, agentic AI, aerospace and semiconductors. The U.S. accounts for 23 of the companies, while China and Korea each added three. Estonia added two, a record for the nation in a single month. Singapore, Germany and Japan each added one new unicorn. The most valuable of the newly minted unicorns were electrical infrastructure company Axiom Solutions International , TypeSafe AI a model developer of Jev, and agentic AI assistant company Manus AI . Familiar names topped the list of investors backing the latest cohort. Andreessen Horowitz has led rounds across seven portfolio companies over time, Sequoia Capital and General Catalyst in four companies and Eclipse three companies from this batch. New unicorns in October 2026 Here are October’s new unicorn companies by industry segment. AI models, assistants and agents TypeSafe AI : San Francisco-based AI model developer TypeSafe AI raised an $870 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation. Andreessen Horowitz led the round, with participation from DCVC and Sequoia Capital. The 2-year-old company develops an AI model Jev for structured decision-making, helping applications automate tasks such as classification, scoring and routing with confidence estimates. Manus AI : Singapore-based AI assistant Manus AI raised $500 million at a $4 billion valuation. Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the round. The 3-year-old company develops general-purpose AI agents that perform tasks including research, browser automation, content creation and software development. Meta agreed to acquire Manus in December 2025, but Chinese regulators intervened and ordered the transaction reversed. Nous Research : Austin-based Nous Research, developer of the Hermes agent, raised a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation. Robot Ventures led the financing, with investors including Nvidia , Microsoft’s M12 , Menlo Ventures and Union Square Ventures . The 3-year-old company develops open-source AI models, agents and infrastructure for AI development and deployment. Nous Research built the open-source Hermes Agent, which it is deploying for businesses. Upstage : South Korea-based Upstage, developer of the open-source Solar model, raised $30 million in Series C funding, reaching $1.5 billion in value. The 6-year-old company develops the Solar language models and document-processing technology that converts unstructured business information into usable data for the future of work. Wabi : San Francisco-based personal AI assistant Wabi raised a $55 million Series A at a $1.25 billion valuation. IVP led the financing, joined by investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Forerunner and Amazon’s Alexa Fund . The 1-year-old company develops an AI personal assistant for everyday activities such as planning trips, coordinating meals and organizing tasks. Town : San Francisco-based Town, a developer of a workforce AI assistant, raised a $108 million Series B at a $1 billion valuation. Forerunner and Menlo Ventures led the round, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, First Round Capital and other investors. The 2-year-old company develops personalized AI assistants that connect with workplace tools across teams to manage email, prepare meeting briefings, organize schedules and complete recurring tasks. Aerospace, defense and space Air Space Intelligence : Boston-based Air Space Intelligence, which makes AI software for national security, raised a $325 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation. Spark Capital led the round, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Citadel Securities , Craft Ventures , Energy Impact Partners and Meritech Capital Partners . The 8-year-old company develops AI software for managing complex physical operations across aviation, defense, energy and logistics. Xona : Burlingame, California-based Xona, which says it’s developing a better satellite navigation system, raised a $250 million Series D at a $2.45 billion valuation. Future Ventures led the round, with participation from Industrious Ventures and Woven Capital . The 7-year-old company says it’s developing a low Earth orbit satellite network to deliver precise positioning, navigation and timing services for applications including defense, transportation and autonomous systems. Firehawk Aerospace : Dallas-based munitions manufacturer Firehawk Aerospace raised a $150 million Series D at a $1.4 billion valuation. Advent International and Rochefort led the round, with Nomi Capital also participating. The 7-year-old company uses additive manufacturing to produce rocket motors, engines and propellant for defense applications. Warhound : Dallas-based Warhound, which breeds genetically optimized service dogs for the military, raised a $200 million seed round at a $1.2 billion valuation. Sequoia Capital led the financing, joined by investors including 8VC 1 , Lux Capital , Breyer Capital and IQT . The less than 1-year-old company was conceived by Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences founder Ben Lamm . Warhound develops genetically optimized dogs by licensing Colossal Biosciences technology and equipping working dogs with Anduril cybernetic technology, for military, law enforcement and emergency response. Reliable Robotics : Mountain View, California-based Reliable Robotics, builder of autonomous aircraft systems, raised a $90 million Series D extension that pushed its valuation above $1 billion. The total Series D funding totaled $250 million with a further $25 million term loan. Nimble Partners led the round. The 9-year-old company develops aircraft automation systems for remotely operated and autonomous flight for commercial and defense use cases. AI data, analytics and coding Labelbox : San Francisco-based Labelbox, a data learning platform, raised a $100 million Series E at a $1.35 billion valuation including equity and a credit facility. Infinitum Partners led the round, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, B Capital and Wipro Ventures among others. The 8-year-old company provides data infrastructure and reinforcement-learning data services for AI laboratories and enterprises. Hex Technologies : San Francisco-based Hex Technologies, a business intelligence platform, raised a $100 million Series D at a $1.2 billion valuation. The round was led by 137 Ventures and Peak XV Partners , with participation from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners , Redpoint and Sequoia Capital. The 7-year-old company has rebuilt business intelligence from scratch for the AI era with context and controls in place with code at the center and data in disparate places.
